'''''Aichryson dumosum''''' is a critically endangered<ref>{{cite web |title=Aichryson dumosum (Lowe) Praeg. |url=https://eunis.eea.europa.eu/species/1691 |publisher=[[European Environment Agency]] |access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref> species of succulent plant of the family [[Crassulaceae]] [[endemic]] to [[Madeira]].

==Description==
''Aichryson dumosum'' is a [[Trichome|glandular]] plant up to {{convert|38|cm|in}} in height, with reddish purple branches. Flowers are {{convert|8|-|10|mm|in}} in diagonal, most with 7 petals, in loose summits. Petals {{convert|4|-|5|mm|in}}, lanceolate, bright golden yellow with a dorsal central rib.<ref name=uma>{{cite web |title=Aichryson dumosum (Lowe) Praeger |url=http://www3.uma.pt/biopolis/planta.php?id=630 |website=www3.uma.pt |access-date=28 November 2020}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
The species is endemic to one single locality on [[Calheta, Madeira|Calheta Municipality]], [[Madeira Island]] and is estimated to have around 50 to 250 individuals occupying only {{convert|100|sqm|sqft}}. It grows in crevices and sheltered areas typical for micro-habitats consisting of an agglomeration of rocks.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" /><ref name=uma />

It is mainly threatened by invasive species, trampling, fires, droughts and landslides.<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />
